front: Who was the king of the Egyptian gods and god of the sun?
back: Ra (also known as Re) — he traveled through the underworld at night and was reborn each morning

front: Which Egyptian god had the head of a jackal and was the god of mummification?
back: Anubis — he guided souls to the afterlife and oversaw the embalming process

front: What was the name of the Egyptian underworld where souls were judged?
back: Duat — the realm through which Ra traveled at night and where Osiris ruled as king of the dead

front: Which goddess was known as the mother of all pharaohs and had a throne-shaped headdress?
back: Isis — goddess of magic, healing, and motherhood, wife of Osiris

front: What happened during the 'Weighing of the Heart' ceremony?
back: The deceased's heart was weighed against the feather of Ma'at (truth); if lighter, they entered the afterlife; if heavier, it was devoured by Ammit

front: Which Egyptian god was murdered by his brother Set and became ruler of the underworld?
back: Osiris — god of the afterlife, resurrection, and fertility

front: What creature had the body of a lion and the head of a human and guarded the pyramids of Giza?
back: The Great Sphinx — believed to represent Pharaoh Khafre

front: Which Egyptian god had the head of an ibis and was the god of writing and wisdom?
back: Thoth — inventor of hieroglyphics and patron of scribes

front: Who was the Egyptian goddess of cats, protection, and fertility?
back: Bastet — originally depicted as a fierce lioness, later as a domestic cat

front: Which god was depicted with the head of a falcon and was the god of the sky?
back: Horus — son of Isis and Osiris, protector of the pharaoh

front: What was the sacred beetle that symbolized rebirth and the rising sun?
back: The scarab (Khepri) — Egyptians believed the scarab beetle rolled the sun across the sky

front: Who was the Egyptian god of chaos, storms, and the desert?
back: Set (Seth) — he murdered his brother Osiris and battled Horus for the throne

front: What is the Book of the Dead?
back: A collection of spells and instructions placed in tombs to help the deceased navigate the afterlife and pass the judgment of Osiris

front: Which goddess had the head of a lioness and was the goddess of war and healing?
back: Sekhmet — her breath was said to create the desert; she was both feared and revered

front: What were canopic jars used for in Egyptian burial practices?
back: To store the preserved organs (lungs, liver, stomach, intestines) of the mummified deceased, each protected by one of the Four Sons of Horus

front: Which Egyptian goddess personified truth, justice, and cosmic order?
back: Ma'at — depicted with an ostrich feather on her head, her feather was used in the Weighing of the Heart

front: Who was the ram-headed god who created humans on his potter's wheel?
back: Khnum — believed to mold children from clay on his wheel before placing them in their mother's womb

front: What was the Benben stone in Egyptian mythology?
back: The primordial mound that rose from the waters of chaos (Nun) at the beginning of creation; pyramids are thought to represent it

front: Which goddess was depicted as a cow or woman with cow horns and a sun disk?
back: Hathor — goddess of love, beauty, music, and joy

front: What was the Eye of Horus and what did it symbolize?
back: A powerful protective symbol representing healing, restoration, and royal power — Horus lost his eye in battle with Set and Thoth restored it

front: Who was Ammit in Egyptian mythology?
back: A demon with the head of a crocodile, front of a leopard, and back of a hippopotamus — she devoured the hearts of the unworthy dead

front: Which god was the patron of craftsmen and was said to have created the world through speech?
back: Ptah — chief god of Memphis, he spoke the world into existence through the power of his heart and tongue

front: What were the Four Sons of Horus?
back: Imsety (liver), Hapy (lungs), Duamutef (stomach), and Qebehsenuef (intestines) — they protected canopic jars

front: Which Egyptian goddess was depicted as a scorpion and protected mothers and children?
back: Serqet (Selket) — she also protected the dead and was associated with healing venomous stings

front: What was the Ogdoad in Egyptian mythology?
back: Eight primordial deities of Hermopolis representing the chaos before creation: Nun/Naunet (water), Heh/Hauhet (infinity), Kek/Kauket (darkness), Amun/Amaunet (hiddenness)

front: Who was the dwarf god that protected households, especially during childbirth?
back: Bes — a jovial, protective deity depicted as a bearded dwarf; his image adorned homes and amulets

front: What role did the Nile River play in Egyptian mythology?
back: It was considered a gift from the gods; its annual flooding was attributed to the tears of Isis mourning Osiris, bringing fertility to the land

front: Which pharaoh attempted to replace all Egyptian gods with a single sun god, the Aten?
back: Akhenaten (Amenhotep IV) — he established a monotheistic worship of the Aten around 1350 BCE

front: What was the significance of the ankh symbol?
back: The ankh represented eternal life; gods were often depicted holding it, and it was one of the most important symbols in Egyptian culture

front: Who was Sobek and why was he worshipped?
back: A crocodile-headed god of the Nile, military prowess, and fertility — Egyptians kept sacred crocodiles in temples dedicated to him
